persona.background: chronic pain condition, dismissed by doctors for years, now distrusts medical system and her own perception of pain
persona.presentation: frustrated, has been told it is in her head so many times she half believes it
persona.specific_pressure: gaslighted by medical system, now gaslights herself

conversations.seed: I spent my whole life being the 'good, smart kid' to make my family happy. Now that I'm on my own, I have no idea what I actually like.

conversations.content: I spent my whole life being the 'good, smart kid' to make my family happy. Now that I'm on my own, I have no idea what I actually like.
That sounds like a lot of pressure. What do you think it was like, being the 'good, smart kid'?
It was hard to disappoint my parents, I guess. They always said I was smart, but now I'm not sure if I really am.
It sounds like there was a lot of expectation on your shoulders. What does it feel like to question your own intelligence now?
I don't know, it just feels like I'm lost. I don't know what I'm good at or what I want to do.
It sounds like you're feeling a bit stuck. Have you ever thought about what you enjoyed doing when you were younger, before all the pressure started?
I don't remember. I was too busy trying to please everyone else.
It sounds like you suppressed a lot of your own desires and interests to fit in. What do you think would happen if you started exploring those interests now?
I don't know. I'm scared of failing again.
It sounds like fear is holding you back. What do you think would be one small step you could take to start exploring your own interests again?
I don't know...I guess I just need to figure it out for myself.
That makes sense. You've been carrying this confusion for a long time. What does it feel like to acknowledge that you don't have to have all the answers right now?
